claims.text: Adding temperature-dependent longitudinal spin fluctuations and chemical short-range order to CALPHAD will significantly improve predictions of melting temperature and entropy of fusion.
The modified framework will outperform models using static magnetic moments and random atomic distributions.
The initial target material is a disordered, random solid solution containing both magnetic and refractory elements.
Finite magnetic moments in Co, Cr, and Ni can be thermally induced by longitudinal spin fluctuations.
The Co magnetic moment rises from about 0.73 μ_B at 100 K to 1.30 μ_B at 900 K in fcc CoCrFeMnNi.
HfTi and TiZr short-range-order pairs form in HfNbTaTiZr simulations.
Short-range ordering in HfNbTaTiZr can produce B2-ordered structures.
The cited HfTi and TiZr pairs have negative pair-interaction parameters indicating that SRO is thermodynamically favorable.
LSFs and SRO regions modify the local electronic structure and free-energy landscape.
Thermal magnetic entropy from LSFs lowers phase-transition free-energy barriers and alters heat capacity.
SRO stabilizes or destabilizes phases by causing departures from ideal random-mixing entropy.
SRO clusters reduce thermal conductivity relative to a random alloy.
The modified method will reproduce experimental melting-temperature and entropy-of-fusion trends in HfMoTaTiZr and CoCrFeMnNi.
The modified method will capture fcc-versus-hcp phase-stability shifts that standard methods miss.
The modified method will capture suppression of intermetallic formation that standard methods miss.
Melting point is modulated by magnetic entropy and SRO-induced lattice distortion rather than being determined solely by average atomic mass or VEC.
Standard CALPHAD and DFT approaches struggle with high-melting alloys specifically because they neglect magnetic and structural correlations.
The method is valid when Co, Cr, or Ni is present and SRO is thermodynamically favorable.
The method may lose accuracy under rapid solidification or for nanoparticles smaller than 10 nm where surface effects dominate.
LSF behavior is documented for CoCrFeMnNi through 1200 K, but extending it to refractory-HEA melting above 2000 K is uncertain.

contradictions.description: The stated computational range ends at 2000 K and is described as reaching near-melting conditions, while the uncertainty field acknowledges that the refractory HEAs of interest often melt above 2000 K.

The validity boundary requires thermodynamically favorable SRO, exemplified by HfTi and TiZr interactions, but the proposed Co-Cr-Ni-W test system contains none of those pairs and no independent criterion is given to establish favorable SRO in that test.
